raw.assessment: The incumbent provides embedded-caption previews in the installation format and retains earlier previews. Its strongest supported case is H1-O7: nine single-correction sessions finished in five to 11 minutes without version uncertainty, so full rendering is not inherently inadequate. Nevertheless, only 20 of 30 sessions met the time target, and four downloads had unexpected captions, including one unexpected video cut. Out-of-order completion and inconsistent mapping records plausibly complicate identification; the observations do not establish whether selection errors, render input errors, or waiting dominate. The sampled 49 processing hours do not establish festival capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an immutable render record binding the selected video and caption hashes, with an editor-readable caption excerpt and request identity shown before rendering and beside the result, would reduce unintended-version downloads.
openings.delta: Identify each preview by its requested inputs rather than requiring reconstruction from caption filenames and completion numbering; preserve the last delivered record and original captions.
openings.prediction: When staging renders finish in reverse request order, editors select the intended pair and its output hashes match the recorded pair. A mismatch despite correct selection would implicate input binding rather than identification alone.
openings.probe: Using fabricated footage on private staging, interleave two video cuts and caption revisions, reverse completion order, and inspect selection plus recorded and actual input hashes.
assumptions: The worker can pin inputs and expose their identities within four engineer-days.
The editor exercise fits one editor-day and processing stays within 80 weekly hours.

openings.claim: Do slow sessions primarily await the intended render, or spend time identifying and reviewing an already available intended preview?
openings.delta: Distinguish a rendering bottleneck from identification overhead before changing when saves trigger rendering.
openings.prediction: A waiting-dominated account predicts late intended-render availability; an identification-dominated account predicts early availability followed by wrong selections or extended comparison. Both may contribute.
openings.probe: Align existing render events with brief staging observations of final edit, intended-output availability, selections, and correct identification; compare repeated edits with single-correction cases.
assumptions: Observation can share the bounded editor exercise above.
Fabricated staging cases test mechanisms but cannot establish the 30-session success target.

raw.assessment: Version mismatch and variable completion order are observed; their causal relationship is unproved. An immediate, trustworthy preview is speculative. These bounded staging probes address complementary accuracy and identification capabilities; neither establishes the 30-session success measure.

openings.claim: A private browser preview could display caption edits immediately while predicting the wording and timing of the eventual embedded-caption delivery.
openings.delta: Replace some full preview renders with synchronized caption overlays. The complete capability depends on immutable video/text pairs, matching caption parsing and timing rules, browser playback accuracy, and demonstrated agreement with the existing embedder. Extract only a partial capability: overlay one supported caption case on retained demonstration footage and compare it with its embedded render.
openings.prediction: For supported cases, editors judge the same wording and cue timing in the overlay and embedded render; any cue disagreement falsifies equivalence for that case.
openings.probe: On private staging, have the two editors compare matched overlays and embedded outputs containing cue boundaries and a single correction. Record cue disagreements, usable-preview latency, engineering time and processing hours. Keep the existing final renderer and last-delivered assets accessible.
assumptions: Browser and embedded caption semantics can be aligned within the four engineer-days and one editor-day; this is unverified.
Staging work plus ordinary processing remains within 80 hours per week.

openings.claim: Would an explicit immutable video-caption receipt remove selection mistakes even when renders finish out of order?
openings.delta: Test identification independently of rendering speed: bind input hashes before enqueueing and show the requested pair beside its completed output.
openings.prediction: With identical completion times, receipts reduce wrong-preview selections compared with sequential completion numbers. No reduction weakens identification as a sufficient intervention.
openings.probe: Replay matched fabricated histories with reversed completion order, counterbalancing the two displays between editors. Verify selected output hashes against intended pairs; measure selection time and errors. Preserve separately accessible last-delivered wording.
assumptions: Private staging can replay these histories within the shared resource budget.
Stored output-to-input associations can be verified rather than inferred from displayed labels.

openings.claim: Immutable input receipts may prevent unintended-version downloads through input binding and clearer identification.
openings.discriminator: Correct selection with mismatched hashes implicates binding; unchanged selection errors weaken identification sufficiency.
openings.probe: Privately replay interleaved cuts/revisions with reversed completion. Counterbalance receipts versus completion numbers at identical timings; show excerpts/request identities; verify actual input hashes and selection time/errors.
openings.uncertainty: Out-of-order completion is not a proven cause; displayed labels alone cannot verify associations.

openings.claim: Separate render waiting from choosing/reviewing an available intended preview.
openings.discriminator: Late intended-output availability supports waiting; early availability followed by comparison/errors supports identification overhead; both may contribute.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints if sharing bounded editor exercise.
openings.probe: Align render events with final edit, intended-output availability, selections and correct identification; compare repeated edits with single corrections.
openings.uncertainty: Nine successful single-correction sessions support incumbent viability; dominant delay and festival capacity remain unknown.

openings.claim: A private synchronized overlay might replace some preview renders if it predicts embedded wording/timing.
openings.discriminator: Any cue disagreement falsifies equivalence for that tested case.
openings.probe: Test one supported caption case on demonstration footage; two editors compare overlay/embedder cue boundaries and one correction; record disagreement, usable latency and resource use.
openings.uncertainty: Requires immutable pairs, aligned parsing/timing and accurate browser playback; broader equivalence remains speculative.

lineage.reason: With Z1; preserves controlled identification comparison.

post_distill.decision: Prioritize shared D1/D2 diagnosis; D3 is exploratory. Keep all assets/computation private, embedded final format and last-delivered original captions accessible. Bound combined work to four engineer-days, one editor-day and 80 processing hours/week. Synthetic staging cannot establish the 30-session success target.
